questions.stem: Which article of the Indian Constitution establishes the Election Commission of India and vests superintendence, direction, and control of elections in it?
questions.explanation: Article 324 establishes the Election Commission of India and vests in it the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice President.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners of India?
questions.explanation: The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which electoral system is used for Lok Sabha elections in India?
questions.explanation: Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections in India use the First Past the Post (FPTP) system — the candidate with the most votes wins, even without an absolute majority. Rajya Sabha uses STV.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner as:
options: A High Court judge, by Parliament's simple majority
A Cabinet Minister, by the Prime Minister
A Supreme Court judge, by impeachment
questions.explanation: The CEC can be removed from office in the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court — i.e., by an order of the President after a motion passed by each House of Parliament by a special majority (impeachment). Other Election Commissioners can be removed on the recommendation of the CEC.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The voting age in India was reduced from 21 years to 18 years by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 reduced the minimum voting age from 21 to 18 years, amending Article 326 of the Constitution.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) were first used on an experimental basis in Indian elections in which state in 1982?
questions.explanation: EVMs were first used experimentally in 1982 in select constituencies in Kerala during the State Legislative Assembly elections. They were rolled out across all constituencies from the 2004 general elections.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Model Code of Conduct (MCC) comes into force when:
options: One year before elections are scheduled
The Election Commission announces the election schedule
90 days before the date of polling
questions.explanation: The Model Code of Conduct comes into effect immediately on the announcement of the election schedule by the Election Commission. It is not a statutory document but is binding as a matter of convention and ECI authority.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Elections to the Rajya Sabha are conducted by which method?
options: Direct election by people of the state
questions.explanation: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies using the Single Transferable Vote (STV) system of proportional representation.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) machines were first piloted in India in September 2013 in which constituency?
questions.explanation: VVPAT was first piloted in the Noksen constituency by-election in Nagaland in September 2013. The ECI gradually scaled its use and deployed it in all constituencies for the 2019 general elections.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Election Commission of India permanently became a multi-member body (with a CEC and two Election Commissioners) in which year?
questions.explanation: While India had two additional Election Commissioners briefly in 1989–90, the multi-member ECI became permanent in 1993 when the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act was enacted.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Anti-defection provisions under the Tenth Schedule are enforced by:
options: Speaker or Chairman of the respective House
questions.explanation: Disqualification on grounds of defection under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha) for the respective House. The ECI is not involved.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The President of India is elected by:
options: Elected members of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha only
All elected MPs and all nominated MLAs
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies
questions.explanation: The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies (and Delhi & Puducherry Legislative Assemblies). Nominated members do not vote.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: In PUCL v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court recognized which election-related right under Article 19(1)(a)?
options: Right to know candidates' criminal and financial background (Right to know)
Right to vote as a Fundamental Right
Right to contest elections without restriction
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court in PUCL (2013) upheld voters' right to know the criminal antecedents, assets, and educational background of candidates as part of the right to freedom of expression under Art 19(1)(a), reinforcing mandatory affidavit disclosure.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'None of the Above' (NOTA) option was introduced in Indian elections following a Supreme Court order in which year?
questions.explanation: NOTA was introduced in 2013 following a Supreme Court order in the PUCL v. Union of India case. It was first used in five state assembly elections in November–December 2013.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner is:
options: 6 years or till age 65, whichever is earlier
questions.explanation: The CEC (and other Election Commissioners) holds office for a term of 6 years from the date of appointment, or until the age of 65 years, whichever comes earlier. They are not eligible for reappointment.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which authority has the power to recognise political parties and allot symbols to them?
questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India has sole authority to recognise political parties as national or state parties and to allot reserved symbols to them under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Election Commission exercises superintendence, direction, and control of elections to all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Office of President and Vice President
questions.explanation: Elections to Panchayati Raj institutions (Gram Panchayats) and Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities) fall under the purview of State Election Commissions established under Article 243K, not the Election Commission of India.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: EVMs were deployed across all parliamentary constituencies in India for the first time in which general election?
questions.explanation: EVMs were used in all constituencies for the first time in the 2004 Lok Sabha General Elections. Prior to that, they were used in select constituencies on a trial basis since 1982.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under which article does the Constitution bar courts from questioning the validity of any election proceeding except by an election petition?
questions.explanation: Article 329(b) provides that no election to either House of Parliament or State Legislature shall be called in question except by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as may be provided for by or under any law made by the appropriate Legislature. (Note: some editions cite this as simply Art 329 — the clause barring court interference mid-election is 329(a).)
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Election Commission of India was established on:
questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India was established on January 25, 1950 — one day before India became a Republic. This date is now celebrated as 'National Voters' Day' every year.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: 'National Voters' Day' is observed on which date every year to mark the founding anniversary of the Election Commission of India?
questions.explanation: National Voters' Day is celebrated on January 25 every year since 2011, commemorating the establishment of the Election Commission on January 25, 1950. It aims to encourage maximum voter registration.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Amendment Act introduced the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law) to the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985 inserted the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution, commonly known as the anti-defection law. It disqualifies members who voluntarily give up their party membership or defy party whip.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 326 of the Indian Constitution provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of:
questions.explanation: Article 326 provides that elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assembly of every State shall be on the basis of adult suffrage — every citizen who is not less than 18 years of age and is otherwise eligible shall be entitled to vote.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to make provisions relating to elections to Parliament (delimitation, qualifications, etc.)?
questions.explanation: Article 327 empowers Parliament to make provision with respect to all matters relating to elections to Parliament and State Legislatures, including preparation of electoral rolls and delimitation of constituencies.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following falls OUTSIDE the jurisdiction of the Election Commission of India?
options: Elections to the President of India
Elections to the Vice President of India
questions.explanation: Elections to Gram Panchayats and other local bodies fall under the State Election Commission (created under Art 243K by the 73rd/74th Amendments), not the Election Commission of India.
questions.subject: Polity
